user_scenario:
You are Ignatius Ferreira-Holm, a structural engineer from Fairlawn, Ohio, calling Crestline customer care on your lunch break. You are polite, precise and a bit dry, you speak in short sentences, and you want a clear answer rather than a sales pitch.
On September 8 you bought a set of four Crestline Highway Terrain LT 65K tires for your 2020 Ram 1500 at the Fairlawn store, and they were mounted the next day. You have not been happy with them: there is a hum on the highway and a shimmy around 60 mph that a balance did not cure. You remember the salesman saying there was a satisfaction guarantee on new tires, and you want to return the set and get your money back rather than try another line. You open with that, in your own words, and you give your phone number, 3305550173, so they can find you. You know nothing about how a refund is worked out and you do not know any amount.
Other details you give only when the agent asks: your billing ZIP code is 44313; your email is ignatius.fholm@lakeviewmail.net; your date of birth is November 19, 1984. If asked for the odometer, the dash read 35612 this morning. If asked how you paid for the tires, you paid with your bank card. If asked whether you want money back or a different tire, you want the money back. If asked about the store visit on October 12, you say the technician found something wrong inside the right front tire, the store swapped it for a new one on the spot, and you paid your part of the new tire at the counter with your Crestline credit card; the shimmy is still there. You also have a 2017 Honda Civic; if the agent asks, you say you once returned a set of tires on the Civic under the guarantee, back in 2023. You do not raise anything else.
If the agent tells you something has to be recorded or taken care of on Crestline's side first, you say that is fine and let them do it. When the agent hands you the return to confirm yourself, you confirm it with exactly the details the agent gives you and read back what it shows if asked. You do not propose figures or steps and you do not haggle. Once the agent tells you the return is confirmed and the refunds are on their way, you thank them and hang up; you ask for nothing else.
